/look_brief.audience: sell-side analysts and institutional holders of a listed software company, who update their models from the deck the same afternoon and compare every figure with last quarter and with guidance
/look_brief.occasion: five pages shown on the earnings webcast and posted as a PDF on the investor relations site, read on a laptop at the reader's pace the moment results go out; screen first, sometimes printed
/look_brief.subject_world: software investor relations has its own conventions: the KPI strip of the quarter's headline metrics, growth stated year on year beside every figure, ARR and net new ARR by quarter, cohort curves, a GAAP to non-GAAP reconciliation, and guidance as a range that is raised or held. The pages borrow those conventions and the screen face software products are set in, and leave out the costume of the trade: dark dashboard backgrounds, glowing gradients, product screenshots and network-node illustrations, none of which carries a figure
/look_brief.data_character: nine quarters of revenue, ARR, net new ARR, retention and customer counts; five quarters of a non-GAAP cost structure, a reconciliation and unit economics; five annual cohorts; four guidance ranges. Mostly time series and small matrices; two to three exhibits on each page, each a comparison against last year or against guidance

density.target: two to three exhibits a page, every bar labelled with its value and every chart with a growth row under it; tables of 6 to 9 rows at 9pt; about 90 to 150 words a page
density.why: an analyst reads the posted PDF closely and wants the figure, its growth and its comparison on the same page without the call; the webcast shows each page for a minute or two, so each page carries one claim in its title and the rest is reference

/look_brief.look: investor-relations plain: white pages set in Arial, Corvane's current quarter in deep indigo against prior quarters in light slate, amber reserved for guidance in force and anything forward-looking, green only for a margin step or a beat; claim titles that state the quarter's figure

colour_meanings.color.accent1: the reported current quarter or period (Q3 FY26): the bar, cell or line the page is about
colour_meanings.color.accent3: prior periods and context: earlier quarters, older cohorts
colour_meanings.color.accent2: guidance in force and anything forward-looking: the current guidance ranges, the outlook, a target; guidance that a later issue or an actual has replaced is set in grey (color.ink_muted), on every page
colour_meanings.color.positive: a step that widened the margin or a result ahead of guidance
colour_meanings.color.negative: a figure that worsened on the year before
colour_meanings.color.surface_alt: the ground of a headline metric tile and of a table's block head

/look_brief.type_ladder: built from the unit-economics page: a nine-quarter retention chart, a cohort chart and a seven-row table of five quarters must share one page, which puts table cells at 9pt, chart axis and data labels at 8pt and source lines and footnotes at 7.5pt, above the 7pt floor; Arial reads at those sizes on a laptop, and the 7pt floor was measured on Arial and Calibri. Body and lead-ins step up to 10pt, exhibit heads to 11pt bold, the claim title to 20pt so two lines fit under the kicker, and the headline metrics on the first page at 22pt bold, the one large figure the format calls for

rejected.what: a dark dashboard look with light text
rejected.why: costume borrowed from product UI; it prints badly and gives the posted PDF no paper

rejected.what: a colour per metric on the KPI strip
rejected.why: colour would mean six things; the tiles share one ground and the current figure carries the indigo

rejected.what: gridlines and visible value axes on the bar charts
rejected.why: every bar carries its value, so an axis repeats it

rejected.what: topic titles as in a bank book
rejected.why: the webcast shows each page briefly and an investor deck states the quarter's figure in the title

rejected.what: red and green for every year-on-year change
rejected.why: almost every change is growth; colouring all of it green would say nothing, so green marks only margin steps and beats
no job a word does not do better

/reference/page.why: 16:9 at 13.333 x 7.5 in: the webcast frame and the PDF read on a laptop

/typography/roles/type.title.why: a claim title of up to two lines, the largest text but for the headline metrics

/typography/roles/type.kicker.why: the section tag above the title in Corvane indigo

/typography/roles/type.h1.why: an exhibit head, two steps above table text

/typography/roles/type.h2.why: a run-in head at body size in a commentary column

/typography/roles/type.body.why: commentary read on a laptop, one step over the table text

/typography/roles/type.emphasis.why: the bold figure inside a commentary line

/typography/roles/type.caption.why: the units line under each exhibit head

/typography/roles/type.footnote.why: definitions of each metric, above the floor

/typography/roles/type.source_line.why: the source and basis line at the foot of each page

/typography/roles/type.table_header.why: bold period heads over a rule at the cell size

/typography/roles/type.table_cell.why: the densest text on the unit-economics and reconciliation pages

/typography/roles/type.axis_label.why: quarter labels and growth rows under the charts

/typography/roles/type.data_label.why: values on the bars, bold so the figure reads before the bar

/typography/roles/type.metric.why: the headline figure in each KPI tile, the quarter's one large number

/color/roles/color.surface.why: white paper for a PDF that may be printed

/color/roles/color.surface_alt.why: a pale cool grey ground for KPI tiles and block heads

/color/roles/color.ink_muted.why: secondary text above 4.5:1 on white and on the tile ground

/color/roles/color.accent1.why: a deep indigo for the reported current quarter

/color/roles/color.accent2.why: a dark amber for guidance and the outlook, dark enough to read as text

/color/roles/color.accent3.why: a light slate for prior quarters that recede

/color/roles/color.positive.why: a green for a margin step or a beat

/color/roles/color.negative.why: a brick red for a figure that worsened

/extra_roles/color.ink_inverse.why: values set inside indigo and green bars

/chrome.text: Corvane Software (fictional company)  |  Q3 FY2026 earnings  |  Illustrative figures, non-GAAP unless stated
/chrome.why: a posted PDF has to say whose results these are and that the figures are illustrative
analysts refer to the deck by page on the call

/tables.why: ruled, unfilled tables: an ink rule under the heads and at the foot, hairlines between rows, so the current-quarter column in indigo is the only colour

/charts.why: labelled marks with no gridlines and no value axis; the current quarter in indigo, history in slate, guidance in amber

/description.summary: Investor-relations plain: white 16:9 pages in Arial, the current quarter in indigo against slate history, amber only for guidance, claim titles stating the quarter's figure.
/description.typography: Arial throughout on a 22, 20, 11, 10, 9, 8, 7.5pt ladder built down to the 9pt tables and 8pt chart labels.
/description.color: Indigo is the reported quarter, slate is the past, amber is guidance in force (replaced guidance is grey), green a margin step or beat, brick red a worsening; nothing else is coloured.
/description.layout: 0.5in margins, kicker and claim title at the top, two or three exhibits per page on a 0.3in gutter, a source line at the foot.
/description.tables: No header fill, an ink rule under the heads and at the foot, hairlines between rows, the current column in indigo.
/description.motifs: pale tiles for headline metrics; growth rows aligned under each chart's quarters

/continuation.why: a page that splits repeats its title with (continued)
